name: publicWeb_redeemAdminToken
description: Validates and redeems a one-time admin token generated by hcportal_generateWebAdminToken. Called by the Next.js /api/admin/auth route to exchange the URL token for a session cookie. Tokens expire after 10 minutes and are deleted on first use (atomic: delete-then-select). Zero rows signals an invalid or expired token; the caller returns HTTP 401.

parameters.name: Token
parameters.description: UUID token string from the URL ?token= parameter. Compared case-insensitively via LOWER(CAST(...))

rowsets.name: RedemptionResult
rowsets.description: Zero rows = invalid, expired, or already-used token (caller treats as 401). One row = valid token, now deleted. On a CATCH block error, zero rows are also returned — errors are swallowed intentionally to prevent leaking internal state.

columns.name: KennelSlug
columns.description: The kennel slug the token was issued for — caller verifies this matches the URL slug before creating the session cookie

sideEffects: Deletes the redeemed row from HC.PublicWebAdminToken (one-time use)

codeSmells.detail: On a runtime error the CATCH block does a ROLLBACK but returns zero rows without any error signal. The caller cannot distinguish a genuine invalid token from a DB error. Acceptable for a security-sensitive path (leaking error detail could aid token-guessing attacks), but worth noting.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove the KennelSlug column — the Next.js route uses it to verify the token's kennel matches the URL
Never change zero-rows = invalid to an error envelope — the caller specifically checks rowset length
Never make the token multi-use — the DELETE must always happen on a valid redemption
